Security bug report: header schemas written with canonical-case header names
are only partly enforced.

Node.js lowercases incoming header names (`X-Admin` arrives as `x-admin`).
Fastify already lowercases the top-level `properties` and `required` of a
route's `headers` schema, but no other position. So a schema like

    headers: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: { 'X-Admin': { const: 'true' }, 'X-Admin-Token': { const: 'server-secret' } },
      dependencies: { 'X-Admin': ['X-Admin-Token'] }
    }

lets `X-Admin: true` through without a token, because the dependency trigger
`X-Admin` never matches the lowercased header.

Fix it so header-name normalization reaches every schema position:

- `dependencies` (array and subschema forms), `dependentRequired` and
  `dependentSchemas`, plus `properties`/`required` inside nested subschemas
  and inside local `$ref` definitions of the headers schema, are all
  lowercased. A canonical-case schema must behave exactly like the
  equivalent all-lowercase schema.
- Normalization must not mutate the schema object the user passed in.
- Header schemas reached through an *external* shared `$ref` (one added with
  `fastify.addSchema`) can't be normalized. For those, emit a new security
  warning `FSTSEC002`, defined and exported alongside the existing `FSTSEC001`
  warning, called with the route's method, url, and the `$ref` value exactly
  as written in the schema (e.g. `'http://example.com/admin-headers#'`).
  Inline schemas and local `$ref`s must not emit it.

'use strict'

const { createWarning } = require('process-warning')

/**
 * Warning codes:
 *   - FSTWRN001
 *   - FSTSEC001
 *
 * Deprecation Codes FSTDEP001 - FSTDEP021 were used by v4 and MUST NOT be reused.
 *                             - FSTDEP022 - FSTDEP025 are used by v5 and MUST NOT be reused.
 * Warning Codes FSTWRN001 - FSTWRN002 were used by v4 and MUST NOT be reused.
 */

const FSTWRN001 = createWarning({
  name: 'FastifyWarning',
  code: 'FSTWRN001',
  message: 'The %s schema for %s: %s is missing. This may indicate the schema is not well specified.',
  unlimited: true
})

const FSTWRN003 = createWarning({
  name: 'FastifyWarning',
  code: 'FSTWRN003',
  message: 'The %s mixes async and callback styles that may lead to unhandled rejections. Please use only one of them.',
  unlimited: true
})

const FSTSEC001 = createWarning({
  name: 'FastifySecurity',
  code: 'FSTSEC001',
  message: 'You are using /%s/ Content-Type which may be vulnerable to CORS attack. Please make sure your RegExp start with "^" or include ";?" to proper detection of the essence MIME type.',
  unlimited: true
})

module.exports = {
  FSTWRN001,
  FSTWRN003,
  FSTSEC001
}

Header-name normalization now reaches every schema position you listed, and `scripts/check.sh` passes: lint, unit (2310 pass, 0 fail) and type tests.

**What changed**
- **`lib/validation.js`**: the old shallow lowercasing is replaced by a recursive `lowerCaseHeadersSchema`. It lowercases the following, and never mutates the user's schema because it works on copies.
  - `properties` keys and `required` entries at every depth, including `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`, `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `items` and `additionalProperties`.
  - The keys and array values of `dependencies`, `dependentRequired` and `dependentSchemas`, and subschema-form `dependencies`.
  - Local `$ref` targets inside `definitions`/`$defs`.
- **`lib/warnings.js`**: new `FSTSEC002`, exported next to `FSTSEC001`. It is called as `(method, url, $ref)` with the `$ref` exactly as written, for any `$ref` that is not local. Inline schemas and local `$ref`s (`#...`, or the schema's own `$id`) don't emit it.
- **`test/headers-case.test.js`**: new tests cover all the forms above against the `X-Admin` / `X-Admin-Token` scenario, plus non-mutation and `FSTSEC002` emission.

**Caveats**
- Custom validator compilers still skip normalization, as they did before, so the new behaviour applies only with the default Ajv.
- The default draft-07 Ajv doesn't know `dependentRequired` or `dependentSchemas`, so the tests register those two keywords through an Ajv plugin.
- Fastify also auto-creates a HEAD route for GET routes, so `FSTSEC002` fires once for each of GET and HEAD.
- I didn't add `FSTSEC002` to `docs/Reference/Warnings.md`, since `FSTSEC001` isn't listed there either.

**What changed**
- **`lib/validation.js`**: the old shallow lowercasing is replaced by a recursive `lowerCaseHeadersSchema`. It lowercases the following, and never mutates the user's schema because it works on copies.
  - `properties` keys and `required` entries at every depth, including `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`, `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `items` and `additionalProperties`.
  - The keys and array values of `dependencies`, `dependentRequired` and `dependentSchemas`, and subschema-form `dependencies`.
  - Local `$ref` targets inside `definitions`/`$defs`.
- **`lib/warnings.js`**: new `FSTSEC002`, exported next to `FSTSEC001`. It is called as `(method, url, $ref)` with the `$ref` exactly as written, for any `$ref` that is not local. Inline schemas and local `$ref`s (`#...`, or the schema's own `$id`) don't emit it.
- **`test/headers-case.test.js`**: new tests cover all the forms above against the `X-Admin` / `X-Admin-Token` scenario, plus non-mutation and `FSTSEC002` emission.

**Caveats**
- Custom validator compilers still skip normalization, as they did before, so the new behaviour applies only with the default Ajv.
- The default draft-07 Ajv doesn't know `dependentRequired` or `dependentSchemas`, so the tests register those two keywords through an Ajv plugin.
- Fastify also auto-creates a HEAD route for GET routes, so `FSTSEC002` fires once for each of GET and HEAD.
- I didn't add `FSTSEC002` to `docs/Reference/Warnings.md`, since `FSTSEC001` isn't listed there either.
